messages.content: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite located at latitude 35.68 and longitude -121.34 for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches.

message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for a location (lat 35.68, lon -121.34) for next 10 days, with daily temperature and precipitation forecasts. They want temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches.

We have no direct tool to fetch weather data. We can use an external API like OpenWeatherMap or WeatherAPI. But we don't have an API key. We might need to use a public API that doesn't require a key. For example, MetaWeather used to be free but is now discontinued. Another option is to use the NOAA API, but that requires registration. There's also the "weatherapi.com" which requires an API key. There's "open-meteo.com" which offers free API without key. Let's check open-meteo.com. It provides weather forecast for lat/lon. It supports daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum. Units can be set to imperial. So we can use open-meteo.com.

Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35.68&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&start_date=YYYY-MM-DD&end_date=YYYY-MM-DD

We need next 10 days. Today is 2026-07-20. So start_date=2026-07-20, end_date=2026-07-29. We need daily temperature max in Fahrenheit and precipitation sum in inches. The API supports units=imperial. So we add &units=imperial.

Thus the request URL: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=35.68&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&start_date=2026-07-20&end_date=2026-07-29&units=imperial

We can fetch this using the browser tool. Then parse JSON. Provide the forecast.

Let's do that.
